name: Glass & Mirrors
tagline: Light, transparency and the illusion of more room
description: Glass buys space that a plan does not have. This section covers safety grades first — toughened and laminated, where the specification is a legal and insurance matter, not a taste one — then decorative glass and the mirror family designers use to stretch small Indian apartments.

materials.name: Clear float glass
materials.blurb: Standard annealed glass for framed and protected applications
materials.description: The baseline product: flat, clear and cheap, but it breaks into dangerous shards. Restrict it to framed, protected positions — never a door, a shower or a low-level panel.

specs.Breakage: Sharp shards — not a safety glass

materials.name: Toughened glass
materials.blurb: Heat-treated safety glass — 4–5× stronger, breaks into blunt granules
materials.description: Thermally tempered so it crumbles instead of spearing. Mandatory for shower enclosures, glass doors, railings and any panel a person could walk into. It cannot be cut after toughening, so all holes and notches must be on the drawing.

materials.name: Laminated glass
materials.blurb: PVB interlayer holds the pane together when it breaks
materials.description: Two panes bonded with a PVB film, so a broken sheet stays in its frame instead of falling. The right answer for overhead glazing, balcony railings and anywhere acoustic performance matters too.

materials.name: Frosted glass
materials.blurb: Acid-etched or sandblasted privacy with full light transmission
materials.description: Obscures the view while passing nearly all the light — exactly what a bathroom door or a home-office partition needs. Acid-etched resists fingerprints far better than sandblasted.

materials.name: Fluted glass
materials.blurb: Vertical ribbed glass — the decade's most requested partition
materials.description: Parallel flutes distort the view into soft vertical bands and catch light beautifully. Used for study partitions, wardrobe fronts and shower screens; toughen it wherever a person could hit it.

materials.name: Reeded glass
materials.blurb: Finer, tighter ribs than fluted — a subtler distortion
materials.description: The narrow-rib cousin of fluted glass, giving a gentler texture that suits smaller panels like cabinet fronts and interior door lights.

materials.name: Tinted glass
materials.blurb: Body-tinted glass that cuts glare and heat
materials.description: Bronze, grey, green and blue tints reduce transmitted light and solar gain — useful on west-facing Indian windows where the afternoon sun is punishing.

materials.name: Lacquered glass
materials.blurb: Opaque coloured glass — the wipe-clean kitchen backsplash
materials.description: Back-painted and baked, giving a seamless coloured surface with no grout to scrub. The default premium backsplash, and a strong wardrobe shutter material in gloss colours.

materials.name: Back-painted glass
materials.blurb: Custom-colour paint on the rear face, matched to the scheme
materials.description: Any RAL or paint shade applied to the back of the glass, so the colour is protected under the pane. Site-painted versions cost less than factory lacquer but are less durable in wet zones.

materials.name: Low-E glass
materials.blurb: Low-emissivity coating that keeps heat where it belongs
materials.description: A microscopically thin metallic coating reflects infra-red, cutting cooling load significantly in Indian conditions. The single most effective glass upgrade for an air-conditioned home.

materials.name: Double-glazed unit (DGU)
materials.blurb: Two panes with a sealed air gap — heat and noise together
materials.description: A sealed cavity between panes cuts both heat transfer and traffic noise, which is why DGUs have become standard in Indian metros. Specify the spacer and gas fill, not just the glass.

materials.name: Decorative glass
materials.blurb: Textured, printed and cast patterns for screens and doors
materials.description: Everything from rolled patterns to digitally printed artwork on glass. Best used where a solid partition would kill the light but a clear one would kill the privacy.

materials.name: Mirror
materials.blurb: Silvered plain mirror — the cheapest way to double a room
materials.description: Standard silvered float in 4–6 mm. Use copper-free, moisture-resistant grades in bathrooms, and always back a large mirror with safety film so a break does not shower the floor.

materials.name: Antique mirror
materials.blurb: Deliberately aged and speckled — softens the reflection
materials.description: Distressed silvering gives a soft, mottled reflection that flatters a room and hides the mess a plain mirror shows. Excellent behind bars and on ceiling panels.

materials.name: Bronze mirror
materials.blurb: Warm bronze-tinted reflection for panelling and wardrobes
materials.description: A bronze tint warms whatever it reflects and reads far less clinical than plain silver. A safe way to use large mirror areas without a room feeling like a gym.

materials.name: Grey mirror
materials.blurb: Smoked grey tint — contemporary and low-glare
materials.description: Cooler than bronze and darker than clear, grey mirror suits monochrome schemes and reduces the brightness bounce in a small room.
